government.note: Parliamentary republic with a unicameral National Assembly. The National Assembly elects the Prime Minister and the President (five-year term, renewable once). The Fundamental Law adopted in 2011 replaced the 1949 constitution and renamed the state 'Hungary' from 2012; constitutional changes need a two-thirds majority. In July 2026 a constitutional amendment ended President Sulyok's mandate.

system.note: From 1990 to 2010 the Assembly had 386 seats, filled by two-round single-member constituencies, regional party lists and national compensation lists (the 2000 start uses this size). The 2011 electoral law cut the Assembly to 199 seats from the 2014 election: 106 single-member seats by first-past-the-post and 93 national list seats (5% threshold, D'Hondt) with partial compensation through transfer votes; pr_share describes this current system. Ethnic minority self-governments can win a preferential list seat (the German minority did in 2018 and 2022). The schema cannot record the change in chamber size; elections from 2014 on record 199 seats. seats_2000 is the result of the May 1998 election; mid-term changes before 1 January 2000 were not checked.
